articleTitle: PLANE CURVE DIAGRAMS AND GEOMETRICAL APPLICATIONS
abstract: We look at plane curve diagrams (f,α), which are given by a plane curve multigerm α : (ℝ, S) → ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and a function on it f:(ℝ, S) → ℝ. We obtain a classification of all such diagrams, where α has<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</inf>-codimension ≤ 2 and f has finite order. Then we define an equivalence between plane curves which we call<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">h</inf>-equivalence and which is determined by the class of the diagram (h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf>, α). Here, h<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</inf> denotes the height function of α with respect to its normal vector. This is an equivalence which not only takes into account the topology of the singularity of α, but also its flat geometry. Finally, we apply our results in order to obtain a classification of all the plane projections of a generic space curve γ embedded in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>

articleTitle: POWERS OF OPERATORS DOMINATED BY STRICTLY SINGULAR OPERATORS
abstract: It is proved that every positive operator R on a Banach lattice E dominated by a strictly singular operator T:E → E satisfies that the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> is strictly singular. Moreover, if E is order continuous then the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> is already strictly singular.

articleTitle: METAPLECTIC OPERATORS ON ℂn
abstract: The metaplectic representation describes a class of automorphisms of the Heisenberg group H = H(G), defined for a locally compact abelian group G. For G=ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</sup>, H is the usual Heisenberg group. For the case when G is the finite cyclic group ℤ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, only partial constructions are known. Here we present new results for this case and we obtain an explicit construction of the metaplectic operators on ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. We also include applications to Gabor frames.

articleTitle: LABELLING THE CHARACTER TABLES OF SYMMETRIC AND ALTERNATING GROUPS
abstract: Let X be a character table of the symmetric group S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. It is shown that unless n = 4 or n = 6, there is a unique way to assign partitions of n to the rows and columns of X so that for all λ and ν, X<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λν</inf> is equal to χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">λ</sup>(ν), the value of the irreducible character of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> labelled by λ on elements of cycle type ν. Analogous results are proved for alternating groups, and for the Brauer character tables of symmetric and alternating groups.

articleTitle: BIALGEBRAS AND CATERPILLARS
abstract: We describe a double construction, which associates a symmetric associative algebra to a bialgebra. We show how a block of a finite group with cyclic defect can be realised via this double construction, after a felicitous choice of bialgebra.

articleTitle: ASYMPTOTICALLY LINEAR ELLIPTIC PROBLEM ON ℝN
abstract: In this paper, we consider the following semilinear elliptic problem:<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p) -\triangle u(x)+\lambda u(x)=f(|x|,u)u, x \epsilon \mathbb{R}^{n}, N\geq2,u\epsilon H^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{N},u\neq0,)$</tex> where f(x, t) tends to p(x) and q(x) ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sup>(ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>), respectively, as t → 0 and t → +∞. We prove that there exist two numbers l and L with L < l such that problem (P) has at least one positive solution for λ ∈ (− l, −L) and has no positive solution for all λ ∉ [−l,−L]. The existence and non-existence of positive solutions for problem (P) at λ = −l and λ = −L are also discussed.

articleTitle: ALPERIN'S CONJECTURE FOR ALGEBRAIC GROUPS
abstract: We prove analogues for reductive algebraic groups of some results for finite groups due to Knörr and Robinson from ‘Some remarks on a conjecture of Alperin’, J. London Math. Soc (2) 39 (1989), 48–60, which play a central rôle in their reformulation of Alperin's conjecture for finite groups.

articleTitle: ON THE ERROR TERMS AND EXCEPTIONAL SETS IN CONJECTURAL SECOND MAIN THEOREMS
abstract: We study the error terms and exceptional sets in conjectural Second Main Theorems in Nevanlinna theory and Diophantine approximation (Vojta's conjecture). In particular, we give a geometric description of the exceptional set in the case of surfaces and the trivial divisor. Examples are given which show that, in general, the exceptional sets in conjectural Second Main Theorems must depend on the parameter ϵ in these conjectures. As a consequence, we obtain counterexamples to a conjecture of S. Lang on the forms of the error terms in conjectural Second Main Theorems.

articleTitle: MULTIPLICATIVE STRUCTURES FOR KOSZUL ALGEBRAS
abstract: Let Λ = kQ/I be a Koszul algebra over a field k, where Q is a finite quiver. An algorithmic method for finding a minimal projective resolution F of the graded simple modules over Λ is given in [E. L. Green and Ø. Solberg, An algorithmic approach to resolutions, J. Symbolic Comput., 42 (2007), 1012–1033]. This resolution is shown to have a ‘comultiplicative’ structure in [E. L. Green, G. Hartman, E. N. Marcos and Ø. Solberg, Resolutions over Koszul algebras, Arch. Math. 85 (2005), 118–127.], and this is used to find a minimal projective resolution ℙ of Λ over the enveloping algebra Λ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">e</sup>. Using these results, we show that the multiplication in the Hochschild cohomology ring of Λ relative to the resolution ℙ is given as a cup product and also provide a description of this product. This comultiplicative structure also yields the structure constants of the Koszul dual of Λ with respect to a canonical basis over k associated to the resolution F. The natural map from the Hochschild cohomology to the Koszul dual of Λ is shown to be surjective onto the graded centre of the Koszul dual.

articleTitle: THE ARITHMETIC BOHR RADIUS
abstract: We study the arithmetic Bohr radius of Reinhardt domains in ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> which was successfully used in our study of monomial expansions for holomorphic functions in infinite dimensions. We show that this new Bohr radius is different from the radii invented by Boas and Khavinson and Aizenberg. It gives an explicit formula for the n-dimensional hypercone (which means n-dimensional variants of classical results of Bohr and Bombieri), and moreover asymptotically corrects upper and lower estimates for various types of convex and non-convex Reinhardt domains.

articleTitle: SCALED ASYMPTOTICS FOR SOME q-SERIES
abstract: This work, investigates the asymptotics for Euler’s q-exponential E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>(z), Ramanujan’s function A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">q</inf>(z), Jackson’s q-Bessel function J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(2)</sup> (z; q), the Stieltjes–Wigert orthogonal polynomials S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(x; q) and q-Laguerre polynomials L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(α)</sup> (x; q) as q approaches 1.

articleTitle: SIMULTANEOUS DIOPHANTINE APPROXIMATION BY SQUARE-FREE NUMBERS
abstract: Let α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …,α<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> ∈ R be ‘not very well approximable’, for example, Q-linearly independent real algebraic numbers. Then there are infinitely many positive square-free integers n such that ‖nα<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">i</inf>‖ << n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−(2/3r)+ϵ</sup>(1 ≤ i ≤ r), where ‖·‖ denotes distance to the nearest integer.

articleTitle: o-MINIMAL ČECH COHOMOLOGY
abstract: We prove the existence of a Čech cohomology theory in arbitrary o-minimal structures with definable Skolem functions satisfying the Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms.

articleTitle: SEMISIMPLE BANACH ALGEBRAS GENERATED BY STRONGLY CONTINUOUS REPRESENTATIONS OF MOORE GROUPS
abstract: We prove that if τ is a strongly continuous bounded representation of a Moore group G on a Banach space X, and if the Arveson spectrum of τ is scattered, then the closure with respect to the weak operator topology in L(X) of the algebra generated by the transforms ∫ <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf>f(t) τ (t)d t with f ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>(G) is a semisimple Banach algebra.

articleTitle: A MULTIPLE GENERALIZATION OF SLATER'S TRANSFORMATION FORMULA FOR A VERY-WELL-POISED-BALANCED 2rψ2r SERIES
abstract: The Jackson integral of type BC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is a multiple generalization of a very-well-poised-balanced <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf>ψ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf> basic hypergeometric series. Based on this fact, a multiple analogue of Slater's transformation formula for the <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf>ψ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2r</inf> series is presented herein. The proposed formula also provides an extension of Gustafson's multiple <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>ψ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> summation formula of type C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>.

articleTitle: BI-ORDERINGS ON PURE BRAIDED THOMPSON'S GROUPS
abstract: In this paper it is proved that the pure braided Thompson's group BF admits a bi-order, analogously to the bi-order of the pure braid groups.

articleTitle: ORTHOGONALLY ADDITIVE POLYNOMIALS ON C*-ALGEBRAS
abstract: We show that for every orthogonally additive scalar n-homogeneous polynomial P on a C*-algebra A there exists φ in A* satisfying P(x)=φ (x<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>), for each element x in A. The vector-valued analogue follows as a corollary.

articleTitle: ON THE SUM OF THE FIRST n PRIMES
abstract: In this note, we show that the set of n such that the arithmetic mean of the first n primes is an integer is of asymptotic density zero. We use the same method to show that the set of n such that the sum of the first n primes is a square is also of asymptotic density zero. We also prove that both the arithmetic mean of the first n primes as well as the square root of the sum of the first n primes are well distributed modulo 1.

articleTitle: THE AVERAGE VALUE OF DIVISOR SUMS IN ARITHMETIC PROGRESSIONS
abstract: Let α(n) denote the Fourier coefficients of cusp forms or the number of divisors of n. Estimates of the type<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sum^*_{b(q)}|\sum_{n\leq X n\equiv b(q)}\alpha(n)-\rm main term |^2\ll_{\varepsilon} X^{1+\varepsilon}$</tex>are shown, uniformly in q ≤ X. The methods can be extended to other arithmetic functions, for example, the number of representations of n as a sum of two squares or k-free numbers. As an application, sums of the type ∑<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n ≤ X</inf>α(n) ψ(n) for any q-periodic function ψ can be estimated non-trivially.

articleTitle: RANK DIFFERENCES FOR OVERPARTITIONS
abstract: In 1954, Atkin and Swinnerton-Dyer proved Dyson's conjectures on the rank of a partition by establishing formulae for the generating functions for rank differences in arithmetic progressions. In this paper, we prove formulae for the generating functions for rank differences for overpartitions. These are in terms of modular functions and generalized Lambert series.

articleTitle: DIVISIBILITY OF MILLER–MORITA–MUMFORD CLASSES OF SPIN SURFACE BUNDLES
abstract: In this paper, we study the divisibility properties of characteristic classes of surface bundles with spin structures. It turns out that the divisibility of the characteristic classes in the non-spin case improves by a power of 2.

articleTitle: ON THE INTEGRAL GALOIS MODULE STRUCTURE OF CYCLIC EXTENSIONS OF p-ADIC FIELDS
abstract: We strengthen results of Miyata on the integral Galois module structure of totally ramified cyclic Kummer extensions K of degree p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> of a p-adic field k. Let c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(K/k) be the first ramification number of K/k, and let c(K/k) be the least non-negative residue of c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(K/k) modulo p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>. Suppose that K is of the form k(α) with α<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pn</sup> ∈ k and val <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>(α−1)>0, (val <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>(α−1), p)= 1. Then the valuation ring of K is free over its associated order 풰 if c(K/k) divides p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</sup>−1 for some m with 1≤m≤n; the converse holds if n= 2; and 풰 is a Hopf order (or a Gorenstein order) if and only if c(K/k) = p<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>−1.

articleTitle: THE DENSITY OF INTEGRAL POINTS ON COMPLETE INTERSECTIONS
abstract: In this paper, an upper bound for the number of integral points of bounded height on an affine complete intersection defined over ℤ is proven. The proof uses an extension to complete intersections of the method used for hypersurfaces by Heath-Brown (The density of rational points on non-singular hypersurfaces, Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. Math. Sci. 104 (1994) 13–29), the so called ‘q-analogue’ of van der Corput's AB process.

articleTitle: ON THE STRUCTURE OF ASYMPTOTIC ℓp SPACES
abstract: We prove that if X is a separable, reflexive space which is asymptotic 퓁<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> for some 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞, then X embeds into a reflexive space Z having an asymptotic 퓁<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> finite-dimensional decomposition (FDD). This result leads to an intrinsic characterization of subspaces of spaces with an asymptotic 퓁<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> FDD. More general results of this type are also obtained. As a consequence, we prove the existence of universal spaces for certain classes of separable, reflexive and asymptotic 퓁<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf> spaces.

articleTitle: POLYNOMIAL NUMERICAL INDEX FOR SOME COMPLEX VECTOR-VALUED FUNCTION SPACES
abstract: We study the relation between the polynomial numerical indices of a complex vector-valued function space and the ones of its range space. It is proved that the spaces C(K, X) and L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>(μ, X) have the same polynomial numerical index as the complex Banach space X for every compact Hausdorff space K and every σ-finite measure μ, which does not hold any more in the real case. We give an example of a complex Banach space X such that, for every k ≥ 2, the polynomial numerical index of order k of X is the greatest possible, namely 1, while the one of X** is the least possible, namely k<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">k/(1−k)</sup>. We also give new examples of Banach spaces with the polynomial Daugavet property, namely L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</inf>(μ, X) when μ is atomless, and C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w</inf>(K, X), C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">w*</inf>(K, X*) when K is perfect.

articleTitle: SPECIAL RAMIFICATION LOCI ON THE DOUBLE PRODUCT OF A GENERAL CURVE
abstract: Let C be a general connected, smooth, projective curve of positive genus g. For each integer i≥0, we give formulae for the number of pairs (P, Q) ∈ C × C off the diagonal such that (g + i − 1)Q - (i + 1)P is linearly equivalent to an effective divisor, and the number of pairs (P, Q) ∈ C × C off the diagonal such that (g + i + 1)Q − (i + 1)P is linearly equivalent to a moving effective divisor.

articleTitle: A NEW METHOD OF PRODUCING FUNCTIONAL RELATIONS AMONG MULTIPLE ZETA-FUNCTIONS
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a new method of producing functional relations among multiple zeta-functions. This method can be regarded as a kind of multiple analogue of Hardy's one of proving the functional equation for the Riemann zeta-function. Using this method, we give new functional relations for multiple zeta-functions. In particular, substituting positive integers into variables of them, we obtain known relation formulas for the multiple zeta-values. Furthermore, applying our method to a certain series involving hyperbolic sine functions, we can obtain certain multiple analogues of the known results given by Cauchy, Ramanujan, Berndt and so on.

articleTitle: DEFORMATIONS OF HYPERCOMPLEX STRUCTURES ASSOCIATED TO HEISENBERG GROUPS
abstract: Let X be a compact quotient of the product of the real Heisenberg group H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4m+1</inf> of dimension 4m + 1 and the three-dimensional real Euclidean space R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. A left-invariant hypercomplex structure on H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4m+1</inf> × R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> descends onto the compact quotient X. The space X is a hyperholomorphic fibration of 4-tori over a 4m-torus. We calculate the parameter space and obstructions to deformations of this hypercomplex structure on X. Using our calculations, we show that all small deformations generate invariant hypercomplex structures on X but not all of them arise from deformations of the lattice. This is in contrast to the deformations on the 4m-torus.

articleTitle: WHEN JORDAN SUBMODULES ARE BIMODULES
abstract: Let be an algebra and let X be an-bimodule. We call a linear subspace Y of X a Jordan-submodule of X if Ay + yA ∈ Y for all A ∈ and y ∈ Y (if X =, then this coincides with the classical concept of a Jordan ideal). When is a Jordan-submodule a submodule? We give a thorough analysis of this question in both algebraic and analytic context. In the first part of the paper, we consider general algebras and general Banach algebras. In the second part, we treat some more specific topics, such as symmetrically normed Jordan-submodules. Some of our results are of interest also in the classical situation; in particular, we show that there exist C*-algebras having Jordan ideals that are not ideals.

articleTitle: ON DAVENPORT–STOTHERS INEQUALITIES AND ELLIPTIC SURFACES IN POSITIVE CHARACTERISTIC
abstract: We show that the Davenport–Stothers inequality from characteristic 0 fails in any characteristic p > 3. The proof uses elliptic surfaces over ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> and inseparable base change. We then present adjusted inequalities. These follow from results of Pesenti and Szpiro. For characteristics 2 and 3, we achieve a similar result in terms of the maximal singular fibres of elliptic surfaces over ℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>. Our ideas are also related to supersingular surfaces (in Shioda's sense).

articleTitle: RIGIDITY OF PERIODIC DIFFEOMORPHISMS OF HOMOTOPY K3 SURFACES
abstract: In this paper, we show that homotopy K3 surfaces do not admit a periodic diffeomorphism of odd prime order 3 acting trivially on cohomology. This gives a negative answer for period 3 to Problem 4.124 in Kirby's problem list. In addition, we give an obstruction in terms of the rationality and the sign of the spin numbers to the non-existence of a periodic diffeomorphism of odd prime order acting trivially on cohomology of homotopy K3 surfaces. The main strategy is to calculate the Seiberg–Witten invariant for the trivial spin<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sup> structure in the presence of such a Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</inf>-symmetry in two ways: (1) the new interpretation of the Seiberg–Witten invariants of Furuta and Fang, and (2) the theorem of Morgan and Szabó on the Seiberg–Witten invariant of homotopy K3 surfaces for the trivial Spin<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sup> structure. As a consequence, we derive a contradiction for any periodic diffeomorphism of prime order 3 acting trivially on cohomology of homotopy K3 surfaces.
